direction.premise: A senior walks through an old personal apartment. Household objects remain tangible and recognizable while memory changes which doorway was behind him.
direction.composition: First-person furniture and narrow kitchen/hall corridors. A highly concentrated optical tunnel appears only during purposeful E/touch peephole inspection, keeping normal play almost completely full-bleed.
direction.shapeLanguage: Old-fashioned lacquered double-leaf wooden doors, glass insets, nonmodular heavy cabinets, brass handles, coat rack silhouettes, Soviet sideboards and inexpensive domestic upholstery.
direction.surfaceAndMaterial: Late Soviet and post-Soviet lived-in domestic realism: varnished glass-panel doors, wall carpet, heavy polished wall-unit with china, enamel kettle, kitchen oilcloth, familiar faded flower wallpaper and herringbone parquet. More readable textile seams, sofa cushions, worn wardrobe moldings, enamel fridge magnets and shallow geometric wall cast shadows. A pale ceramic breaker board and a battered plug-in hotplate have visually meaningful switch states.
direction.paletteLogic: Desaturated nicotine cream, brown wood and muted sage replace teal industrial corridors; isolated warm brass marks objects and danger appears as faint rusty red.
direction.typography: Small utilitarian location and objective labels in play; larger compressed worn theatre-poster title only in the initial nocturnal menu.
direction.signature: The Soviet apartment opens onto a second recognizable place through a real brass peephole. A stairwell grocery net and family photograph unite remembered life inside and outside; topology remains safe and closed until a future walkable chapter.
direction.distinction: Memory is participatory: recognize distorted furniture, tune a radio, connect family objects and resolve a personally meaningful ending. Never a standard gun-vs-monsters progression.
direction.spatialRationale: A small persistent HUD leaves almost the entire view for walls and belongings. Separate left/right thumb surfaces keep first-person navigation usable in portrait.

comparisons.spatialDifference: First-person WebGL field with spatial walls and fog replaces a framed top-down tile arena.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Continuous physical walking and looking replace swipe-by-tile turns.

comparisons.spatialDifference: No action-toolbar or heavily composed weapon frame; nearly screen-filling desolate geometric hallways.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Exposure, retreat and collecting anchors rather than projectiles and execution.

production.renderer: Custom offline WebGL1 Soviet apartment plus a separate peephole-view 3D stairwell mesh (lift, neighbor door, stair steps, notices, grocery net). Fixed procedural albedo atlas; no external artwork dependency.
production.focalAsset: The opening apartment itself: seeded room assignments, furniture, patterned walls and physical door frames plus a personally authored wooden-door icon.

motion.character: Measured walking inertia and subtle gait synchronized to movement; rounded enemies sway slightly, avoiding ceaseless random camera wobble.
motion.action: The same E/touch action checks the peephole, then leaves its view; active look mode disables movement, pistol and other competing controls until exit.
motion.anticipation: A shadow at a doorway or the sound of furniture shifting warns of a changing remembered room before it can be revisited.
motion.response: Real E/touch interactions change kettle/plug and breaker state, audible latches, radio availability and electrical ambient illumination; the flashlight remains independently powered.
motion.followThrough: After a glance away, a room may have moved its door; the next visit resolves into a visibly different furniture arrangement while objectives remain accessible.
motion.interruption: Pointercancel and focus loss always reset movement; pause saves state and freezes pursuit without claiming the user has died.
motion.reducedMotion: Reduce-motion disables head-bob while keeping navigation, textures, enemy visibility and action states intact.

evidence.expectedChange: The apartment menu closes to reveal a furnished first-person interior with functional movement, aim, weapon and interactable objects.

architecture.primaryVerb: Walk through the mutable Soviet flat, recognize misplaced memories, collect family keepsakes, tune a Bakelite radio and choose whether to leave.
architecture.physicalFeedback: Walking and looking navigate room geometry, door hinges follow actual collision, the radio tuning dial and audible channel change together, and narrative recognition changes story and stress state.
architecture.spatialRationale: Low-priority HUD hugs the top/phone edges while the inhabited apartment occupies full screen; interactive inventory is a temporary overlay.

comparisons.spatialDifference: A single personal apartment seen through the protagonist's eyes replaces an overhead army map, region borders and tactical interface panels.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Exploration and inventory-based storytelling differ from troop movement, resource management and turn resolution.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Eye-level rooms with old wallpaper, a household door and full-bleed perspective are unlike Trafficity's miniature overhead streets and legible road graph.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Walking, recalling family objects and fending off private hallucinations replaces drawing tactical routes for little delivery vehicles.

comparisons.spatialDifference: A furnished eye-height domestic interior and working door replace the stylized fixed-grid tactical dueling board and UI lanes.
comparisons.interactionDifference: The player navigates in real time through changing personal rooms and collects narrative objects, not submitting simultaneous tactical actions on a five-by-five battlefield.

comparisons.spatialDifference: The view opens inside an inhabited, enclosed old apartment with low ceiling, textile furniture and brass door, not a grotesque labyrinth of organic membranes.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Collecting family objects and navigating an unreliable known home with limited subjective combat replaces a fast arcade shooter through fleshy procedural levels.

comparisons.spatialDifference: A continuous 3D maze seen through eye-height perspective replaces a flat single-screen competitive gravity or pulling arena.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Player explores branching hallways and survives fleeting pursuers through spatial awareness, instead of issuing short symmetric competitive pushes.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Eye-level corridor depth and fullscreen personal horror replace the tiny cooperative warehouse seen as a planar two-avatar puzzle.
comparisons.interactionDifference: One person navigates and turns their viewpoint with continuous independent controls rather than splitting axes between two human players.

comparisons.spatialDifference: A fully furnished 3D post-Soviet apartment with old doors and a tabletop radio replaces a paper manuscript and framed communal writing surface.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Survival movement and exploration have immediate spatial consequences rather than alternating between text drafting and chapter reveal.

comparisons.spatialDifference: A lived-in first-person Soviet apartment differs from a tabletop image restoration and comparison gallery.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Continuous dual-stick physical exploration and real-time survival replaces restoring and voting on altered artworks.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Eye-height exploration of private family rooms with 1980s furniture differs from a broad overhead historical village simulation.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Every swipe turns the character's eyes while movement can provoke stalkers, rather than selecting or observing historical households.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Perspective through domestic furniture and worn wallpaper replaces a bright drawing workbench.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Walk, turn and hide from silhouettes instead of drawing strokes, filling regions and managing layers.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Full-bleed first-person 3D environment replaces a flat framed dungeon viewport.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Continuous twin-stick navigation replaces discrete map steps.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Deep volumetric corridors replace overhead time-echo puzzle grid.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Moving and surviving while forgetting spaces replaces placing route echoes.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Eye-height corridor navigation replaces top-down abbey and bottom bell plate.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Free movement with 3D flashlight replaces pivoting a fixed lamp.

comparisons.spatialDifference: A continuous first-person Soviet family apartment with physical radio, furniture and localized perception differs from Perekos's compact pixel-art wizard-duel battleground.
comparisons.interactionDifference: The player navigates rooms, collects memory fragments and tunes a radio to resolve a personal story instead of composing competitive conditional rune chains and resolving 1v1 spell tactics.
